quizGuardRationale: Pairs are direct and symmetric through the app, not transitive. Original baseline exclusion declarations remain untouched.
Expansion/extension labels overlap in widening, lengthening and development senses despite practical differences; the pairs do not declare every object freely substitutable.
Scholarship/learning labels need checks against financial scholarship and knowledge/ability. An English scholarship ambiguity does not make 学術 or 学力 a student grant.
角度/釣る protects English noun/verb angle polysemy without claiming the Japanese words are synonyms.
学年/成績 protects school-year versus assessed-mark grade polysemy; university faculty does not mean every use of mental faculty.
可決/通過 shares actual legislative passage; 可決/通行 also protects English physical/legislative passage polysemy.
重なる/重ねる and accumulation/repetition comparisons retain their different grammatical viewpoints; broad English stack/repeat labels can remain ambiguous.
飾り/飾る protects English noun/verb ornament polysemy; decorative accessories overlap but equipment accessories need not be ornaments.
かしこまりました pairs protect broad acknowledgment and English certainly labels, not a universal substitution rule among response registers and truth assertions.
Exact-title deduplication already keeps 各自 and 一人一人 apart; no redundant direct guard is required.
sourceAccessLimits: Actual-entry receipts describe author inspection and are not fresh independent reviewer retrieval.
Original source fields and complete principal families are retained even when glosses cross readings or selected coverage omits a specialist sense.
The selected comparison families are complete entries, not exhaustive dictionary or synonym coverage.
各地 receives only a sourced N2 field. 火山 receives that field and a link on its existing 火口 comparison. Stable identity, reading, title, original exclusions and prior teaching are preserved.
Reciprocal N2 links are added for 各/各自, 角/角度 and 算/掛け算 without deleting prior readings, including 算's source-only そろ qualification.
Written 拡, 充, 張, 率, 可 and 飾 remain in word metadata despite absent kanji cards; no broken links or speculative kanji/stroke cards are introduced.
Native-first 掛け算 uses wago plus mixed-reading, with its native stem and voiced on-reading explicitly explained.
No dictionary ordering, absence of a priority flag or original-list gloss is treated as measured modern usage frequency.
